scenario: AITA for telling my mom she was a bad mother? | So this is kind of a two part thing. A while back, I made my mother upset because of a couple different things I said while out with her. She was saying something about how she didn't believe in doctors and that my siblings literally beg her to go and she still puts off taking them as long as possible. I told her that's not okay, that she did that to me and I nearly died (I was hospitalized for weeks, and spent several months on bedrest recovering), and that if she keeps that up one of us really might die some day because of her. She didn't take that too well, but ended up dropping it and brushing it off as no big deal. Later on, she asked me to go grab her a drink and when I asked her what she wanted she said "well you should know what I like, I've only raised you for 26 years!" And I told her no, I do not know what you like, my grandparents raised me, I still don't know anything about you. She got upset and started crying and said "what's your problem!? This is the second time today that you've been mean to me and tried to make me seem like a bad person!" I told her I'm not trying to be mean I was just saying it's not cool to not take your kid to the doctor and that I'm not going to know anything about her since I didnt grow up with her. We ended up going home shortly after and went out again the other night, a few weeks later. Well I got my brother a phone because they kept taking his (that a different family member pays for) and I wanted him to have his own, so I made it clear they can keep his other one and this one is STRICTLY for him. Well I found out they've been taking and using this one too, so when I saw her I told her, seriously, I dont want to take the phone back because I don't want him to be punished for what you're doing, but I will take it back if you don't stop stealing it from him. That is HIS that I'M paying for, not you, it is not yours to touch, it's already bad enough that you keep all his work money at least don't touch his phone. She got upset and starting yelling and crying saying I need to stop treating her like a bad mother, and I told her well to be honest she kind of IS one. She had a meltdown and started sobbing and said well fine, I don't need you in my life anyways, and left without me. Now my family is saying I shouldn't of treated her like that even if she wasn't that great to me. AITA?

I was hospitalized for weeks and had to spend several months on bed rest recovering. That's a big deal, and it's something that's stuck with me. Then, there's the whole thing with my phone and my brother's phone. I bought him a phone because they kept taking his, and I wanted him to have his own. I made it clear that this phone was strictly for him, but I found out they've been taking and using it too. When I confronted her about it, I told her that if she didn't stop stealing it, I would take it back. She got upset, started yelling and crying, and said I shouldn't treat her like a bad mother. I told her honestly that she kind of is one. She had a meltdown, started sobbing, and said she didn't need me in her life anyway, then left without me. Now, my family is saying I shouldn't have treated her like that, even if she wasn't that great to me. So, am I in the wrong here? Is it okay to tell someone they're a bad parent, especially if they've caused you harm? First, I need to understand the context better. My mom has a history of not believing in doctors, which led to me being hospitalized. That's a serious issue because it put my life at risk. She also didn't take my siblings to the doctor even when they begged her. That's neglectful and shows a pattern of behavior that's harmful. Then, the phone situation. I bought my brother a phone to ensure he had his own, but she's been taking it. When I confronted her, I set boundaries by saying I would take it back if she continued. She reacted emotionally, and I told her she's a bad mother. That escalated things, and she left, saying she didn't need me. So, is it right or wrong to tell someone they're a bad parent? On one hand, I feel justified because her actions have caused me significant harm. On the other hand, calling her a bad mother might have been hurtful and could have contributed to the conflict. I also need to consider the impact of my words. While I was expressing my feelings and setting boundaries, labeling her as a bad mother could have been perceived as attacking her character rather than addressing specific behaviors. It might have made her feel defensive and led to her leaving, which could have been avoidable. Moreover, my family is advising me not to treat her like that, even if she wasn't great to me. They might be concerned about maintaining family relationships and not letting past issues dominate our interactions. They might believe that it's better to communicate in a way that focuses on specific actions rather than making personal attacks. In the end, I need to weigh the importance of expressing my feelings honestly against the potential consequences of damaging our relationship further. It's a tough balance between being truthful and maintaining a respectful relationship. Maybe a better approach would have been to address her specific actions without labeling her as a bad mother. For example, I could have said, "I'm hurt that you didn't take me to the doctor when I was younger, and I'm concerned about your attitude towards seeking medical help." This way, I'm expressing my feelings without attacking her character. Similarly, in the phone situation, I could have focused on the behavior of taking my brother's phone and how it affects him, rather than calling her a bad mother. This might have led to a more constructive conversation and prevented the emotional breakdown. So, while I understand why I felt the need to tell her she's a bad mother, it might not have been the most effective way to communicate my concerns. It could have been better to address her specific actions and express how they've affected me, rather than making a general judgment about her parenting. In conclusion, while my feelings are valid, the way I expressed them might have been more hurtful than helpful. It's important to communicate my concerns in a way that focuses on specific behaviors and their impact, rather than making personal attacks. This approach could lead to a more constructive dialogue and help maintain our relationship, even if it's challenging.
